2. The petitioner as the plaintiff filed other class suit No. 92 of 1997 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Parbotipur, Dinajpur against the defendant-respondents for declaration of title in the suit land. The plaintiff's case,' in brief, that there is a 'beel' after the name of Naya Mollah who excavated the 'beel' and the predecessors-in-interest of the plaintiff, had been using the water of the 'beel' for a long time for irrigation. The said 'beel' had been recorded in the name of Zaminder Profullha Kumar and others from whom, one Ram Charit Shah took pattan, who was a big jotedar. But the predecessors of the plaintiff were owners of other lands encircling the 'beel' and for irrigation, they prayed to Ram Charit Shah for the said 'beel' who allowed the prayer and settled the said 'beel' to Shamiuddin Shah and Saditullah Shah. At the time of preparation of C.S. record, the predecessors of the plaintiff were not present and as such, it was wrongly recorded in their names as জলকর instead of প্রজাস্বত্ব and subsequently, they came to know after inquiry that S.A. record has been prepared in the name of Government as Khas land. After that, they inquired of the P.R.R. record where they found that Khantian No. 1186 was prepared in the name of Solman Shan, Bafaj Shah and Jakiya Bewa, the heirs of the plaintiff's predecessor as of প্রজাস্বত্ব The plaintiff further stated that they came to know that defendant No. 1 Government of Bangladesh, leased out the suit land to Parbatipur Branch of Grameen Bank and the plaintiff claimed that meanwhile they acquired tenancy right in the suit land but defendants denied his claim and as such, the title suit has been filed by the plaintiff for declaration. 

 3. The defendants contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material statements made in the plaint. Their case, in short, is that the disputed 'beel' is a big one comprising 9.12 acres of land and it is a natural one. The C.S. record was prepared in Khas Khatian No. 1 in the name of Zaminder Biddut Kumar Sarker and the plaintiff never possessed the suit land and they have no right and title in the suit land, And as such the suit for declaration of title is liable to be dismissed.
